q: Calculate the mean for volunteer A.
Identify the anomalous result. State how you would calculate C’s mean, with a reason.
C trial 2 (140 °) is far from C’s other two. Repeat it, or leave it out: (122 + 123) / 2 = 122.5 °.
Calculate the range of A’s trials and state what it shows.
131 − 128 = 3 °: a small range, so the method gives repeatable readings for this person.
A student concludes that range of motion falls with age. Evaluate this conclusion.

The trend supports it (17-year-olds 122–135 °, 45 years 118 °, 70 years 106 °). But there is only one person at each older age, the young volunteers vary by 13 °, and fitness, injury or sex could explain the difference. Many more volunteers per age group are needed.
Suggest two ways to make the goniometer readings more reliable.
Any two: mark the joint centre and bone landmarks on the skin; the same person takes every reading; volunteers lie in the same position; standard warm-up; more repeats.
